judged_text: The collective multi-host push `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op when neither eventType.destinationCalendar nor organizerUser.destinationCalendar exists, because evt.destinationCalendar was just set to null two statements earlier. This is the exact scenario the PR title claims to fix: a COLLECTIVE event where the organizer has no destination calendar but team members do — the members' destinationCalendars are collected into teamDestinationCalendars and then silently discarded, so only one (or zero) calendar events are created for a collective booking.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when both `eventType.destinationCalendar` and `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` are falsy (`destinationCalendar: ... : null`). Immediately after, for COLLECTIVE team events the code does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. With `destinationCalendar === null`, the optional-chained `push` is a no-op, so any member calendars accumulated into `teamDestinationCalendars` are discarded and won’t be used downstream (e.g., `createAllCalendarEvents` only iterates when `destinationCalendar && destinationCalendar.length > 0`). This matches the reported scenario: organizer has no destination calendar but other team members do.
